text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty P1 -> DNS resolver failures observed from EU edge resolvers (eu-west). Multiple customer 5xx spikes; start ~10:12 UTC. Paging @oncall and eng-networking.

Dan Li: I'm oncall, taking this. Quick triage: who can run dig against model-eu.redwood.ai against 1.1.1.1 and 8.8.8.8 and our Route53 names? Also paste any sample 5xx payloads.

Ben Ortiz: running quick checks now, pasting outputs.
```
$ dig @1.1.1.1 model-eu.redwood.ai A +short
;; -> SERVFAIL

$ dig @8.8.8.8 model-eu.redwood.ai A +short
54.12.23.101
54.12.23.102

$ dig @ns-1234.awsdns-56.co.uk model-eu.redwood.ai A +short
54.12.23.101
54.12.23.102
TTL: 1800
```

Carla N'Guyen: Observability: eu inference endpoints error rate peaked ~47% 5xx, average latency up ~200ms. Top affected customers: search-saas, docparser. Sample curl failure:
```
curl https://model-eu.redwood.ai/v1/predict -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -d '{}'
{"error":"upstream fetch failed (DNS failure)"}
```

Marta Singh: Looks like resolver-side SERVFAIL from Cloudflare edge resolvers in EU. Route53 authoritative answers are healthy, but many client resolvers hitting CF are returning SERVFAIL or stale cached entries. My recommendation: trigger Route53 failover/weighted shift to direct traffic to us-east as a temporary mitigation, and open a support ticket with Cloudflare immediately. This will reduce customer impact while CF resolves their resolver fleet.

Dan Li: Agreed. Ben, can you do the Route53 change (weighted/failover) and create a health check? I'll coordinate support with Cloudflare and post an update to customers.

Ben Ortiz: Doing a quick change via AWS console/CLI. Command I'm using:
```bash
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z3EXAMPLE --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"CREATE","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"model-eu.redwood.ai","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"eu-failover-us-east","Weight":100,"TTL":300,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"34.201.5.77"},{"Value":"34.201.5.78"}]}}]}'
```
Created a health check pointing at the us-east LB. Applying now.

incident-bot: Route53 change submitted -> propagation in progress. Monitoring metrics.

Carla N'Guyen: Quick metric update: 5xx dropped from 47% -> 9% within 4 minutes. Some customers still see failures (likely cached resolvers returning SERVFAIL or stuck to old answers). We should note cached resolver TTL behavior in comms.

Marta Singh: Opened Cloudflare ticket CF-54212 with dig logs and traceroutes. CF acknowledged they're seeing resolver errors in EU and have an internal rollback in flight. ETA 15-30m per support. I've requested a high-priority status update and asked for the impacted POPs list.

Dan Li: Good. Action items while we monitor: 1) eng-sre + eng-networking to own the postmortem, 2) evaluate adding secondary authoritative NS (reduce single-provider risk), 3) pre-bake lower TTL records for critical endpoints in case of future flips, 4) update runbook with a Route53 quick-failover play.

Ben Ortiz: Notes: TTL on the authoritative record was high (1800) which slowed natural failover for some resolvers. We set the weighted record with TTL 300 for quicker shift. Also started a Cloudflare resolver purge request (they can flush their caches on certain POPs).

Dan Li: Handoff: I'll stay for another 30m then hand to night oncall Marta. Marta, please watch for regressions and ensure we have CF status updates. Postmortem owners: Carla + Marta.

Marta Singh: Acknowledged, taking the handoff. I'll follow up on ticket CF-54212 and update the incident channel with timestamps.

Ben Ortiz: :thumbsup: I'll follow up in the morning to validate DNS health in all regions and propose adding a geo-fallback to our infra in the runbook.

incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated (traffic shifted; error rates back to normal range). Monitoring for 60m. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/dns-failover.

Dan Li: Closing the urgent paging loop. Leaving notes for postmortem: root cause likely CF resolver fleet instability in EU POPs, mitigation was Route53 weighted failover to us-east + CF cache purge request. Follow-ups: secondary NS, runbook TTL defaults, and customer comms draft.

pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged -> responders notified.

Carla N'Guyen: Adding final log snippet for postmortem:
```
2026-02-18T10:12:34Z eu-inference LB - upstream_dns_error - client=10.9.8.7 request_id=abc123
2026-02-18T10:16:50Z Route53 change applied, traffic shifted to us-east
2026-02-18T10:19:05Z error_rate down to 3%
```

Dan Li: Thanks everyone. Postmortem owners please schedule follow-up and link to incident ticket CF-54212 in the writeup.

Marta Singh: Will do.

[end of thread]
